assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration correction in the transmission electron microscope turned a decades-old theoretical limit (Scherzer) into routine sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy of atoms, interfaces and defects across materials science, physics and chemistry. It is a clear, original invention with enormous and lasting impact, and it fits the 'discovery or invention' criterion directly.
assessment.attribution: Rose (theory of the corrector design), Haider (building and demonstrating the hexapole-based corrector in the TEM) and Urban (the Juelich implementation and application to atomic-scale materials imaging) form a coherent three-person configuration. The supplied credit omits other pioneers of aberration-corrected STEM, so the allocation is not free of dispute.
assessment.maturity: Commercially deployed for roughly two decades and independently confirmed by many groups worldwide; the technology is stable and the recognition is timely, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit for aberration-corrected STEM (a parallel development) is not in the supplied names and could complicate the configuration.
I note a professional proximity to this field and would flag it for a conflict check rather than treat it as evidence of merit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, based on the magic-wavelength idea, deliver fractional uncertainty near 1e-18 and have opened fundamental-physics tests, relativistic geodesy and a path to redefining the second. A clean, well-defined invention with transformative precision-measurement impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated early clocks; Ye drove the accuracy and stability records. A two-person prize is natural, though other clock groups (ion clocks, other lattice groups) have contributed.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs have reproduced and surpassed the performance; the interpretation is stable and the topic is mature, with the redefinition of the second still pending.
uncertainties: Relation to prior recognition of optical frequency combs and ion clocks must be considered by the committee.
Allocation relative to other lattice-clock pioneers is not settled by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The recollision (three-step) picture and its quantum theory underpin high harmonic generation and attosecond pulse generation, and thus the whole field of attosecond science. The concept is simple, original and has far-reaching experimental consequences, including imaging of molecular orbitals.
assessment.attribution: Corkum's 1993 recollision model is the decisive conceptual contribution; Lewenstein and colleagues supplied the quantum theory (strong-field approximation) that made it quantitative. Corkum alone might be the stronger core, and I would treat Lewenstein as a secondary but defensible addition.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed through experiments for three decades. Timing is good, although the 2023 prize already honoured attosecond pulse generation, so the committee must judge whether this is a distinct discovery or an overlap.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 attosecond prize needs careful judgement.
Other theorists (Kulander, Schafer and others) contributed to the recollision picture and are not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened an entire field of moire quantum materials, with correlated insulators and unconventional superconductivity tunable in a single device. Original, rapidly influential and conceptually clear because of a predictive flat-band theory.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle and flat bands; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the experimental discovery of correlated states and superconductivity. The first author of the experimental papers is not among the credited names, which creates an attribution difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many groups, but the microscopic origin of the superconductivity is still debated; recognition is somewhat early though the experimental facts are secure.
uncertainties: Junior experimental contributors are not in the credited names, and the theory-experiment split may be contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Hubbard model with tunable parameters, giving quantum simulation of Mott insulators and strongly correlated phases with single-site resolution. A major conceptual and experimental advance.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and co-workers) proposed the atom-lattice Hubbard realisation; Greiner and Bloch demonstrated the Mott transition and developed microscopy; Esslinger and Cirac also have strong claims. Five names are credited, so any three-person choice leaves out important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Well-confirmed across many labs; the field is mature though the practical scientific payoff of simulation is still developing.
uncertainties: Selecting three of five credited names is contentious.
Overlap with earlier prizes on cold atoms and BEC.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators established a new class of quantum matter with protected edge and surface states, from the Kane-Mele proposal to the experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state. Deep, original and highly influential.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the theory; Molenkamp's HgTe experiment confirmed the quantum spin Hall effect, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction, who are not in the credited names. Hasan's 3D observations are a further claim. The configuration is therefore delicate.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many groups, and well after the 2016 topological-phase prize the committee must decide whether this is sufficiently distinct. The interpretation is very stable.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions.
Uncredited theorists (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) affect fair attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unexpected discovery of high-temperature superconductivity in iron pnictides in 2008 opened a second major family of high-Tc materials and stimulated large experimental effort on correlated superconductors.
assessment.attribution: The initial discovery in LaFeAsO(1-x)Fx is clearly traceable to Kamihara and Hosono, so attribution is clean, though a prize for the discovery of a material may be viewed as narrower than a concept.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced very rapidly and with Tc raised above 50 K; yet the pairing mechanism is still debated, and applications are limited.
uncertainties: Whether a materials discovery without a settled mechanism has enough conceptual weight.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, and later giant TMR in MgO barriers, underlies modern magnetic sensors and memory. It is a materials-and-interface physics advance with large technological impact.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin (and Yuasa) achieved giant TMR in MgO with coherent tunnelling. The supplied credit omits Yuasa and others, and the 2007 GMR prize partially overlaps in territory.
assessment.maturity: Technologically mature and well confirmed; the theory of coherent spin-dependent tunnelling is established. Timing is reasonable, but novelty relative to the GMR prize may be questioned.
uncertainties: Credit for MgO-based giant TMR is split among groups not all in the supplied names.
